MUQATIL:8:36-37/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:8:36-37/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:8:36-37/r3.claim: God distinguishes disbelievers from believers and piles the disbelieving Badr leaders together in Hell; these were the ones who fed the fighters.

MUQATIL:8:36-37/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:8:36-37/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:8:36-37/r4.claim: The named Badr leaders include Abu Jahl, the sons of Hisham and Rabi'a, and other Quraysh chiefs; they are the losers.

AKHFASH:v1p349/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p349/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p349/r4.claim: ليميز may come from doubled ميز; some lighten it as يميز from ماز يميز, which is the reading Akhfash adopts.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p179#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p179#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p179#2/r1.claim: Yarkumuhu means piling the bad things into a heap, one upon another.

TUSTARI:8:37/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:8:37/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:8:37/r1.claim: The evil comprises disbelief, hypocrisy, and major sins; the good is faith, whose ranks include prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and the righteous.

TUSTARI:8:37/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:8:37/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:8:37/r2.claim: God piles the evil together in layers according to their sins, as shown by the hypocrites’ lowest level in Hell.

TAB-FULL:v11p175/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p175/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p175/r1.claim: God separates unbelievers, the evil ones, from believers, the good ones, by placing the faithful in Paradise and the unbelievers in Hell.

TAB-FULL:v11p175/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p175/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v11p175/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the separation is between the people destined for felicity and those destined for misery.

TAB-FULL:v11p175/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p175/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v11p175/r3.claim: Al-Suddi explains the distinction as separating believer from unbeliever.

TAB-FULL:v11p175/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p175/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p175/r4.claim: The evil are piled together, with some carried atop others, forming a heap; ركام describes a gathered, dense mass, as in the cloud image at 24:43.

TAB-FULL:v11p175/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p175/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v11p175/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses the piling as gathering the evil ones together, some atop others.

TAB-FULL:v11p175/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p175/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p175/r6.claim: The singular khabith describes a collective, but أولئك returns to the plural spenders; they are losers because they traded wealth for punishment and earned humiliation by fighting the Prophet and believers.

ZAJJAJ:v2p412/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p412/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p412/r1.claim: The sorting distinguishes believers’ spending in obedience from disbelievers’ spending in disobedience; r-k-m means piling one thing on another, and their accumulated spending is placed upon them as punishment in Hell.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وابن عامر وأبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p305/r2.claim: These readers read ليميز with fatḥa on yāʾ and no gemination; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī use ḍamma and gemination.

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1699/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1699/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1699/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says God distinguishes believers from disbelievers as the pure from the impure.

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1699/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1699/r2.speaker: شمر بن عطية
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1699/r2.claim: Shumr ibn Atiyya says God separates righteous deeds done for Him from worldly things, then gathers up the whole world and casts it into Hell.

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1699/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1699/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1699/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says the impure will be piled together and placed in Hell.

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1699/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1699/r4.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1699/r4.claim: Muqatil says the losers are people of Hell in the Hereafter.

NAHHAS:v2p185/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p185/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p185/r3.claim: The phrase is purposive accusative; يميز is intensive and later verbs coordinate.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p152/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p152/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p152/r1.claim: The passage gives competing forms of ليميز: a light reading is connected with ماز يميز and the heavy form with ميزته فتميز; its reciter list appears internally inconsistent, naming Hamza and al-Kisai and then all others for the same heavy form.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p152/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p152/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p152/r2.claim: The heavy form is supported by Quranic تميز: objects separate through repeated movement and agitation; the phrase من الغيظ depicts the intensity of the boiling, angry fire.

SULAMI:v1p266#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p266#4/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p266#4/r1.claim: Purification separates sincere people from show-offs, believers from unbelievers, and obedient people from sinners.

SULAMI:v1p266#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p266#4/r2.speaker: محمد بن الفضل
SULAMI:v1p266#4/r2.claim: Good wealth is wealth from which God's due has been paid; impure wealth is wealth whose due was withheld.

SULAMI:v1p266#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p266#4/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p266#4/r3.claim: Good wealth is spent to relieve the poor when they are in need; impure wealth is imposed on them when they have no need, occupying their thoughts.

SULAMI:v1p266#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p266#4/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p266#4/r4.claim: Wealth spent in obedience is good, and wealth spent in corruption is impure.

THALABI:v4p355/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p355/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p355/r1.claim: The gathering separates unbelievers from believers, placing believers in gardens and unbelievers in the Fire.

THALABI:v4p355/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p355/r2.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v4p355/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says the evil and good distinguished are evil and righteous deeds, rewarded with Hell and Paradise respectively.

THALABI:v4p355/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p355/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p355/r3.claim: The Kufans, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Aʿmash, and ʿIsa read the verb with shadda, a reading preferred by Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim.

THALABI:v4p355/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p355/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v4p355/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the contrast as good spending for God versus evil spending for Satan, with the latter piled into Hell.

THALABI:v4p355/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p355/r5.speaker: مرة الهمداني
THALABI:v4p355/r5.claim: Murra al-Hamdani says prior divine knowledge distinguished believers created good from unbelievers created evil; obedience or refusal manifests this distinction.

THALABI:v4p355/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p355/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p355/r6.claim: Rakama means piling things densely like a gathered cloud; the singular predicate first follows khabith, then the plural ‘those’ returns to the earlier people who spent.

THALABI:v4p355/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p355/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p355/r7.claim: The losers are those whose bargain failed: they bought punishment in the next life with their wealth.

THALABI:v4p355/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p355/r8.speaker: محمد
THALABI:v4p355/r8.claim: Muhammad says ‘if they desist’ means desist from shirk; if they return to fighting, the earlier pattern of prophetic victory and unbeliever destruction, as at Badr, applies.

THALABI:v4p355/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p355/r9.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ الرازي
THALABI:v4p355/r9.claim: Yahya ibn Muʿadh hopes that pure monotheism which erases earlier unbelief can also erase later sins.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p317/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p317/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p317/r3.claim: The foul distinguished from the good may mean unlawful from lawful, wealth with God's dues unpaid from wealth whose dues were paid, or spending on sin from spending in obedience.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p317/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p317/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p317/r4.claim: God gathers the foul together in the afterlife although it was scattered in worldly life; rakam means piling one thing atop another, as in 24:43.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p317/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p317/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p317/r5.claim: Money in Hell may become a punishment, as in 9:35, or accompany its owners in humiliation because they used it to gain power for sin.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p144#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p144#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p144#2/r1.claim: One interpretation identifies the impure and pure as disbelievers and believers; the purpose clause attaches to the disbelievers' being gathered to Hell, separating the wretched from the blessed.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p144#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p144#2/r2.speaker: مرة الهمداني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p144#2/r2.claim: Murra says God distinguishes believers, whom He created pure in prior knowledge, from disbelievers, whom He created impure; the impure are joined together for Hell.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p144#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p144#2/r3.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p144#2/r3.claim: Al-Layth defines r-k-m as piling one thing over another until it forms a heap, like piled sand or clouds; exegetes say the impure are gathered into Hell like a mass of clouds.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p144#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p144#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p144#2/r4.claim: The singular verb refers back to the singular khabīth, explaining the singular grammatical form.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p144#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p144#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p144#2/r5.claim: Ataa's report from Ibn Abbas says this community's judgment was deferred to the Last Day, unlike earlier nations; believers hidden in disbelievers' loins are then separated, as in 36:59.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p144#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p144#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p144#2/r6.claim: On this report, the impure are packed into Hell and constrained like a garment folded or beads threaded onto a string, with forelocks joined to feet, as in 69:32.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r1.claim: A second interpretation takes the pure and impure as believers' spending in jihad and disbelievers' expenditure against Muhammad; al-Kalbi says evil and good deeds are repaid with Hell and Paradise.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd calls spending for God's cause pure and spending in Satan's cause impure; the latter is cast into Hell and its owners told to join it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq and Ibn al-Anbari choose the spending interpretation: God separates what believers spend in obedience from what polytheists spend in disobedience.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r4.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r4.claim: Asked why insentient wealth is thrown into Hell, Abu Bakr answers that God can make their unlawful wealth a means of pain, as in 9:35.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj likewise says the wealth is piled in the fire and made to burn its owners, as the heated hoards brand them in 9:35.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r6.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r6.claim: A second answer is that Hell displays the worthlessness of wealth they prized and boasted of; a prophetic report depicts the adorned world asking to be given to a divine ally and being sent to the Fire as contemptible.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p146/r7.claim: The purpose clause li-yamīza attaches to the preceding statement that they will spend their wealth and then regret it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p147/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p147/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p147/r1.claim: The losers are the disbelievers who spent in Satan's service: their bargain failed because they bought afterlife punishment with their wealth.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:36-38/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:36-38/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:36-38/r3.claim: The gathering distinguishes people doomed to misery from people destined for happiness; the wicked are unbelievers grouped together and piled up in Hell.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:36-38/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:36-38/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:36-38/r4.claim: The wicked are unbelievers as a class, joined to one another and heaped like piled clouds before being put in Hell.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:36-38/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:36-38/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:36-38/r5.claim: They are losers because they purchased God's punishment in the afterlife with their money.

JISHUMI:v4p2921/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2921/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2921/r6.claim: Tamyīz is separating or distinguishing two things; khabīth is what is poor or bad, opposite ṭayyib, which is good and may mean pleasant or lawful.

JISHUMI:v4p2921/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2921/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2921/r7.claim: Rukām is a mass stacked layer upon layer, like piled clouds, sand, or mud; the verb means placing one thing over another.

JISHUMI:v4p2921/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2921/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2921/r8.claim: The singular masculine pronoun in فيجعله refers back to khabīth; أولئك is plural because it refers to الذين كفروا at the opening.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356/r1.claim: One view identifies the evil with disbelievers and the good with believers, destined respectively for Hell and Paradise.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356/r2.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets the evil and good as wicked deeds and righteous deeds, with their respective recompenses in Hell and Paradise.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356/r3.claim: A further view distinguishes spending for Satan’s cause from spending for God’s cause.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356/r4.claim: The evil is piled together, as a dense mass of clouds is gathered.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356/r5.claim: The losers are the disbelievers who spent their wealth, losing their trade because they bought punishment in the Hereafter.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p207#3/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p207#3/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p207#3/r10.claim: On the main reading, the lām attaches to ‘they will be gathered’; under the alternative, it attaches to ‘it becomes regret.’ The reading ليميز is lightened.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p207#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p207#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p207#3/r7.claim: The disbelievers among them are gathered to Hell, since some others accepted Islam well.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p207#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p207#3/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p207#3/r8.claim: The verse distinguishes the unbelieving group from the believers and heaps the vile together until they are piled up, as in the image of piled crowds.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p207#3/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p207#3/r9.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p207#3/r9.claim: Alternatively, it separates the ill-gotten money spent against the Prophet from the good money spent by Abu Bakr and Uthman to support him, then consigns the former to Hell with its owners.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r1.claim: These readers pronounce ليَميز with an open yāʾ and kasra on mīm, from ماز; a rare reading انمازوا and Abu Zayd's line illustrate the verb's form and its passive-like separation.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r2.claim: They read ليميز with a prefixed ḍamma, open mīm, and doubled yāʾ, from ميّز meaning to separate; 67:8 uses تميز for things separating.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r3.claim: They identify the vile as disbelievers and the good as believers.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r4.claim: On that interpretation, the purpose clause attaches to the disbelievers being gathered: God distinguishes them by gathering them together and casting them into Hell; losers are those whose effort failed and who ended there.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r5.speaker: ابن سلام والزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r5.claim: They identify the vile as the wealth polytheists spent obstructing God's path and the good as believers' spending in God's path.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r6.claim: On this view, the purpose clause attaches to their being overcome: despite their spending, the disbelievers are defeated, so God distinguishes the groups by abandoning the vile and supporting the good.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r7.claim: A report says God will bring out on Resurrection Day the wealth that was charity or an act of devotion, then order the rest thrown into the Fire.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r8.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r8.claim: Hasan says the disbelievers are punished through that wealth; al-Zajjaj compares this to the Qur'anic threat that wealth will brand its owners.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p526/r9.claim: On both interpretations, piling the vile together means collecting, joining, and compacting its scattered parts; ركم means to make dense, as in سحاب مركوم and Dhu al-Rumma's verse.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r1.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r1.claim: Abu Ali explains يجعل الخبيث as يلقي, 'casts'.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r2.claim: Under the wealth interpretation, the losers are hypocrites among the disbelievers; the word loss suits them both financially and in other respects.

TABRISI:8:36-37#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:36-37#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:36-37#2/r1.claim: One reading of separating the bad from the good distinguishes unbelievers' spending from believers' spending, then piles all the unbelievers' expenditures together and punishes them in Hell as in 9:35.

TABRISI:8:36-37#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:36-37#2/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:8:36-37#2/r2.claim: Abū Muslim says God distinguishes unbelievers from believers: in this world through victory, triumph, recognized names, and special rulings, and in the next through reward and Paradise.

TABRISI:8:36-37#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:36-37#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:36-37#2/r3.claim: Another interpretation has the bad people piled atop one another in Hell, packed together like a heap of clouds; the phrase “make it in Hell” means He admits them there.

TABRISI:8:36-37#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:36-37#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:36-37#2/r4.claim: These people lose themselves because they traded spending their wealth in disobedience for punishment in the afterlife.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p355#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p355#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p355#2/r1.claim: They read limayiza without gemination; Hamza and al-Kisa'i use a geminated form, and both are Arabic variants.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p355#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p355#2/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p355#2/r2.claim: The lām in limayiza connects to the earlier “they will spend it” phrase.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p355#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p355#2/r3.speaker: ابن جرير الطبري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p355#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the lām connects to the phrase about gathering them to Hell.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p355#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p355#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس عن ابن أبي طلحة والسدي ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p355#2/r4.claim: One interpretation is distinguishing the people of bliss from misery, or believers from unbelievers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p355#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p355#2/r5.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p355#2/r5.claim: Another interpretation is distinguishing good deeds from bad deeds.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p355#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p355#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p355#2/r6.claim: Another interpretation separates spending for God's cause from spending for Satan's cause.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356/r1.claim: Rakama means piling one thing on another; the resulting heap is called rukam.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356/r2.claim: If “the bad” means unbelievers, they are piled on one another in Hell.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356/r3.claim: If “the bad” means their wealth, one view says it is thrown into fire to punish its owners, as in the warning of 9:35.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356/r4.claim: Another view says wealth they revered in life is thrown into fire to show its humiliation, as with the sun and moon.

RAZI-FULL:v15p129/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p129/r1.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v15p129/r1.claim: Muqatil and al-Kalbi say the spending passage was revealed about twelve leading Quraysh who financed the army at Badr.

RAZI-FULL:v15p129/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p129/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v15p129/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid say it concerned Abu Sufyan financing war against Muhammad at Uhud; al-Kashshaf reports he hired two thousand Abyssinians and other Arabs and spent forty uqiyyas, each of forty-two mithqals.

RAZI-FULL:v15p129/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p129/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p129/r3.claim: The disbelievers spent to block others from following Muhammad, God's path, even if they did not understand their own purpose in those terms; the spending ultimately became regret because it failed and they were defeated, as 58:21 promises.

RAZI-FULL:v15p129/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p129/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p129/r4.claim: The verse specifies those who remained disbelievers because some of the original spenders later became Muslims; its wording appears to restrict their gathering to Hell, and Razi says their spending brings only worldly regret and frustration plus severe punishment in the afterlife.

RAZI-FULL:v15p129/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p129/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p129/r5.claim: One interpretation says God separates the evil unbelieving party from the good believers, then piles the evil together like the crowded mass in 72:19; those refers to the evil party.

QURTUBI-FULL:8:37/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:37/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:37/r9.claim: ‘Distinguishing the foul from the good’ means separating disbeliever from believer, or more generally sorting all kinds of deeds, spending, and other things.

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:37/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:37/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:37/r1.claim: The impure and pure may mean disbelievers and believers, or corruption and soundness; the purpose clause can attach to gathering, victory, or the spending which becomes a regret.

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:37/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:37/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:37/r2.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Yaqub read the verb as tamyiz, which is more intensive than simple separation.

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:37/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:37/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:37/r3.claim: The impure are heaped together until crowded upon one another, or the spending is joined to the disbelievers to increase their punishment like hoarded treasure.

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:37/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:37/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:37/r4.claim: The final reference points either to the impure faction or to the spenders, who lose themselves and their wealth completely.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p64#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p64#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p64#4/r1.claim: The purpose clause attaches to resurrection: God separates the unbelieving faction from the believing faction; Hamza and Kisāʾī have the recorded reading.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p64#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p64#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p64#4/r2.claim: God piles the wicked together, gathers them all, and casts that faction into Hell; they lose themselves and their wealth.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p316/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p316/r10.speaker: السدي ومقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p316/r10.claim: Al-Suddī and Muqātil take the evil and good as unbelievers and believers, separated into the miserable and the happy.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p316/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p316/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p316/r11.claim: Zamakhshari paraphrases the distinction as the evil faction of unbelievers being separated from the good faction of believers.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p316/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p316/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p316/r12.claim: Making the evil into a heap means gathering them together so none can escape; jaʿala may mean transforming them or casting them into Hell.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p316/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p316/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p316/r7.claim: The verse describes the final fate of disbelievers who remain unbelievers through death; the wording repeats because some who spent against Islam later converted.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p316/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p316/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p316/r8.claim: The lām in li-yamīza attaches to yuḥsharūn; khabīth and ṭayyib can describe people or money, and this echoes the spending in the preceding verse.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p316/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p316/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p316/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the evil and good as the people destined for misery and happiness.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r1.speaker: ابن القشيري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r1.claim: Ibn al-Qushayr says God distinguishes the groups by delaying punishment of this community until the Resurrection, allowing believers to emerge from unbelievers' descendants; on this view the distinction occurs in worldly history.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r10.claim: He compares their spending to a failed business deal: they sacrifice their most valuable possession for God's punishment, the greatest possible loss.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r11.claim: The source notes variant readings and forms of the verb meaning to distinguish, including a rare reading for separate yourselves and a poetic witness cited by Abū Zayd.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r2.speaker: ابن سلام والزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r2.claim: Ibn Sallām and al-Zajjāj interpret the evil as the wealth spent by polytheists such as Abū Sufyān and Abū Jahl to oppose the Prophet, and the good as believers' spending, including Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r3.claim: On the wealth interpretation, Ibn ʿAṭiyya attaches the purpose lām to يغلبون; Zamakhshari instead attaches it to the later promise that spending will become regret.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r4.claim: Zamakhshari links lām to ثم تكون عليهم حسرة and explains that God will abandon the corrupt and support the righteous, with the casting into Hell as further punishment.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r5.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r5.claim: Al-Hasan takes the casting of wealth into Hell as one of the punishments, like branding owners with their hoarded treasure.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r6.claim: Other readings identify the evil and good as spending on sins versus obedience, unlawful versus lawful wealth, or wealth whose zakat was withheld versus wealth whose zakat was paid.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r7.claim: A broad interpretation makes the evil deeds; piling them up means sealing them and hanging them like collars around their makers' necks in Hell.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r8.claim: If evil means the money spent against the Prophet, one explanation says it is thrown into Hell to show its humiliation, just as the sun and moon are cast there to shame their worshippers.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p317/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers the people interpretation: the evil are the disbelievers already under discussion and the good are believers, and the ending identifies the unbelievers as the losers.

SAMIN-DURR:8:37#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:37#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:37#2/r1.claim: فيركمه coordinates with the preceding subjunctive; ركم means piling something over something until it forms a heap, like sand or clouds.

SAMIN-DURR:8:37#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:37#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:37#2/r2.claim: The expression سحاب مركوم in الطور 52:44 provides a Qur'anic usage of the root for piled clouds.

SAMIN-DURR:8:37#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:37#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:37#2/r3.claim: المرتكم can mean the main road, named for the crowding of passersby and their traces.

SAMIN-DURR:8:37#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:37#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:37#2/r4.claim: جميعا is either a circumstantial accusative or, according to some grammarians, an emphatic.

SAMIN-DURR:8:37/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:37/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:37/r1.claim: The purpose lam in ليميز attaches to يحشرون; the earlier dispute about the verb's reading was treated under آل عمران.

SAMIN-DURR:8:37/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:37/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:37/r2.claim: يجعل may be causative and take two objects, or mean casting and take one; in either parse بعضه is partitive apposition.

SAMIN-DURR:8:37/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:37/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:37/r3.claim: With causative يجعل, على بعض is the second object; with the casting sense it completes the verb, like casting belongings one over another.

SAMIN-DURR:8:37/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:37/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:8:37/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa instead allows على بعض to be a circumstantial phrase meaning the vile things are piled with some above others.

SAMIN-DURR:8:37/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:37/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:37/r5.claim: The rare reading وانمازوا occurs in يس 36:59; Abu Zayd cites a verse using وانمزت as evidence for this word family.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p53/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p53/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p53/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq’s account, citing Ibn Abbas, says Quraysh traders funded war after Badr to avenge relatives killed there, and the spending passage was revealed about them.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p53/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p53/r2.speaker: مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير والحكم بن عتيبة وقتادة والسدي وابن أبزى
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p53/r2.claim: Mujahid and others say the passage concerned Abu Sufyan’s spending to fight the Prophet at Uhud; al-Dahhak says it concerned the people of Badr.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p53/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p53/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p53/r3.claim: Although the occasion may be specific, the warning applies generally to disbelievers spending to block truth; their money becomes regret, they are defeated and humiliated in this world, and face lasting punishment in the Fire.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p54/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p54/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p54/r1.claim: The wicked-versus-good distinction separates the people of felicity from the people of misery.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p54/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p54/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p54/r2.claim: The distinction is between believer and unbeliever.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p54/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p54/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p54/r3.claim: One possible distinction occurs in the Hereafter, separating associators from their partners and separating groups at resurrection.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p54/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p54/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p54/r4.claim: Alternatively, this distinction appears in worldly conduct, visible to believers, as obedience in fighting enemies versus disobediently hanging back.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p54/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p54/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p54/r5.claim: On the worldly reading, the causal lām explains why God enables unbelievers to spend wealth obstructing the path: the ordeal distinguishes people.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p54/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p54/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p54/r6.claim: God gathers the wicked together, piling them up as rakkama means collecting things upon one another, as with piled clouds; they are the losers in both worlds.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r1.claim: The Qur'an challenges those who claimed they could produce its like: if sincere, they would have done so, even after claiming it was not uniquely true.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r2.claim: The reference to whistling and clapping shows that self-proclaimed masters of eloquence could not answer the Qur'an's height and descended to animal noises.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r3.claim: If they could rival the Qur'an through speech, they would not substitute costly spending, bodily suffering, and death for that challenge, with eternal disgrace as the result.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r4.claim: The gathering of disbelievers distinguishes wicked people from good ones: this is just toward disbelievers and a favor to believers.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r5.claim: The wicked are heaped together, with the repetition clarifying a real piling and tight joining like piled clouds, before being cast into Hell, a place of distress and confinement.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r6.claim: They alone are the losers because their loss is complete: at the gathering they bought their own destruction with their wealth.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p205#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p205#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p205#2/r1.claim: The impure and pure may mean disbelievers and believers, corruption and righteousness, or the money spent by polytheists against the Messenger and money spent by Muslims to support him; the final reading attaches the purpose to making their spending a regret, not to their being gathered.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p205#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p205#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p205#2/r2.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Yaʿqub read ليميز with doubled yāʾ, a more intensive form than ليميز; an anomalous reading has the criminals told to separate themselves.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p205#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p205#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p205#2/r3.claim: The root يركمه means to pile together like a piled cloud, sand, or army; if impure means disbelievers, it depicts their crowding, while corruption means sorting each corrupt kind together.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p205#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p205#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p205#2/r4.claim: If the impure means hostile spending, God gathers that money to cast its owners into Hell and brand their faces and sides; a broader reading joins evil unbelievers with their evil money to increase their torment and regret.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p205#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p205#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p205#2/r5.claim: The demonstrative may point to the impure group or to spenders who remained unbelievers; its distance signals their extreme depravity, and they are complete losers of themselves and their wealth.

ELMALILI:8:36-38/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:36-38/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:36-38/r4.claim: God separates good from evil so the promised distinction for the pious is realized and the good and bad become clearly distinct.

ELMALILI:8:36-38/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:36-38/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:36-38/r5.claim: God piles the evil together, adds their evil wealth to them, heaps it all up densely, and casts the whole into Hell; these are the losers.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p341/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p341/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p341/r6.claim: The relative clause identifies unbelief as the reason for their worldly and afterlife punishment and applies to those who have not abandoned it before events arrive.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p341/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p341/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p341/r7.claim: The purpose phrase attaches to their being gathered: separating wicked people from good people is one of the reasons for gathering unbelievers in Hell.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p341/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p341/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p341/r8.claim: Most readers vocalize ليميز from māza; Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Ya'qub, and Khalaf use the intensive form from mayyaza; attributing the action to God makes the readings equivalent.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343/r1.claim: Sensory filth extends metaphorically to moral vileness; here it describes corrupt souls and deeds, as unbelief distorts belief and action while faith leads oppositely.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343/r2.claim: The preposition من in the phrase 'the wicked from the good' marks separation, as discussed at 2:220.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343/r3.claim: Collecting all wicked people together is another reason for Hell: it separates them publicly from the good, exposes concealed unbelief, humiliates them, and makes them suffer as a heap.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343/r4.claim: Rukm means piling something above what is beneath it, as in the description of clouds at 24:43.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343/r5.claim: The demonstrative says their prior traits make them deserving of the description as losers, since they forfeit both worldly and afterlife benefits.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343/r6.claim: The restrictive pronoun is hyperbolic: their loss is so complete that everyone else's loss counts as none by comparison.

TABATABAI:8:35-37/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:35-37/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:35-37/r6.claim: Khabith and tayyib are opposites; distinguishing separates something from what conflicts with it and joins it to what agrees, while piling means stacking parts together.

TABATABAI:8:37-39/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:37-39/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:37-39/r1.claim: The verse explains why disbelievers’ strenuous campaign against God’s light fails: divine order separates evil from good, gathers evil into Hell, and sends good toward Paradise.

TABATABAI:8:37-39/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:37-39/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:37-39/r2.claim: The image closely matches the water-and-foam parable: falsehood vanishes while what benefits people remains, expressing the universal law that each branch joins its root.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p4/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p4/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p4/.claim: God gathers the evil elements together and consigns them to Hell.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p44.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p44.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p44.claim: The furqān in the Hereafter is God's separation of good from evil; rakm means piling in layers, and the layered heap burns intensely, subtly depicting disbelievers who aided each other becoming fuel for one another.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p44.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p44.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p44.claim: The losers lose in both lives: their worldly spending earns no reward and brings regret and defeat, while in the Hereafter they are cast into Hell like a heap of filth.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:36/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:36/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:36/r4.claim: Muslims sought to follow God’s path and establish a life pleasing to Him; polytheists tried to block them at great cost, but their sacrifices ended in failure and suffering.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:36/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:36/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:36/r5.claim: The outcome separates good from evil and pure from impure, with freely chosen paths ending in God’s pleasure and Paradise or His wrath and Hell, then and always.

QIRAAT-ER:8:37:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:8:37:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:8:37:2#1/r1.claim: Form II portrays God as thoroughly sifting the foul from the wholesome, item by item.

STUDYQURAN:8:37/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:37/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:8:37/r1.claim: The plain sense is that God separates the bad from the good in the Hereafter.

STUDYQURAN:8:37/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:37/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:8:37/r2.claim: The language recalls 3:179, which also speaks of God separating bad from good.

STUDYQURAN:8:37/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:37/r3.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:8:37/r3.claim: IK allows that the separation may occur in this world, as at Uḥud when battle separated the Prophet's sincere followers from hypocrites.
